headline: Snap pitches itself as a kind, creative, purpose-driven camera company — with belonging and DEI language that surged in 2020–21, retreated sharply in 2023, then partially recovered.
identity: Snap has consistently valued kindness, creativity, and a civilizational-sounding mission — 'contribute to human progress by empowering people to express themselves, live in the moment, learn about the world, and have fun together' appears verbatim across every year from 2018 to 2026. DEI and inclusion language, however, has not been steady: it expanded dramatically from 2018 (near-absent) to a peak in 2020–21 (inclusion z-scores above 1.2, explicit terms like 'LGBTQ+,' 'unconscious bias training,' and 'allyship'), then collapsed in 2023 to its lowest point in the dataset (inclusion z-score –1.76, only three thin chunks captured), before recovering to above-average levels by 2025. The altruism signal followed a similar arc, peaking in 2020 and hitting a trough in 2023 (z-score –2.14), suggesting 2023 was a year of significantly reduced careers-page content overall.
fit: You might be a good fit if you are drawn to a culture that explicitly names 'kind, smart, and creative' as its operating values, are comfortable with aspirational DEI framing (the copy leans on 'belonging' and perspective-taking rather than structural commitments), and want to work on camera and augmented-reality products framed as tools for human connection rather than pure technical achievement.

sections.heading: The Stable Core: Kind, Smart, Creative
sections.body:
From 2018 through 2026, Snap's careers copy has anchored on three named values — kind, smart, and creative — and a fixed mission statement about human progress. The phrasing of these values did shift once: in 2021 the copy updated 'We Are Kind: we listen from the heart, think empathetically, and help each other grow' to 'we operate with courage, show empathy, and instill trust through honesty and integrity,' and 'We Are Creative' moved from 'challenge the status quo' to 'gracefully manage ambiguity, cultivate innovation.' The 2021 rewrites added performance-adjacent language ('make high-quality decisions,' 'strategic mindset') that persisted through 2025, pushing performance z-scores from –0.22 in 2018 to a peak of 1.30 in 2025.

Techno-optimism language was low throughout most of the period but rose noticeably from 2024 onward, driven by explicit augmented-reality copy: 'Snap Augmented Reality enables creators around the world to revolutionize the way we create, explore, and play' appears in 2024, 2025, and 2026, lifting the z-score from –1.79 in 2023 to +1.24 in 2026.

sections.heading: DEI: A Surge, a Collapse, and a Reframe
sections.body:
DEI language was essentially absent in 2018 (all chunks coded 'absent' in the register field). It expanded sharply in 2020, when a dedicated Diversity, Equity & Inclusion section appeared with explicit demographic terms — 'race and gender, LGBTQ+, disability, age, socio-economic status' — and process commitments like 'unconscious bias training' and 'allyship training.' The inclusion z-score hit 1.21 in 2020 and 1.28 in 2021. Terms 'bias' and 'lgbtq' both disappeared after 2021.

In 2022 the register shifted: the explicit demographic list dropped out, and the highest-scoring inclusion quote became a process description of 'Snap Council' — a listening practice — rather than a DEI statement. By 2023 the careers page was extremely thin (only 3 chunks), and all DEI-adjacent scores fell to multi-year lows. From 2024 onward the copy returned to aspirational framing ('We believe that when we can see the world from other's perspectives, we come to understand why DEI is so essential') and by 2025–26 introduced 'belonging' as the primary frame, with the headline claim 'We believe in hiring the most talented team members and creating an environment where everyone belongs' — a formulation that pairs meritocracy and inclusion in a single sentence, reflected in that quote's near-equal inclusion (0.70) and meritocracy (0.63) scores.

sections.heading: Wellbeing and Altruism: Community-Oriented but Uneven
sections.body:
Wellbeing language was below-peer-average in 2018–19, rose through 2020–22 (driven by ERG descriptions and the Snap Council belonging narrative), then dropped sharply in 2023 before recovering to above-average by 2025–26. The recurring 'Snap-a-Wish' program — 'Have a teammate going through a tough time? Lend them a hand' — is the one wellbeing signal present even in the sparse 2023 data, suggesting it is a durable fixture.

Altruism scores follow a similar pattern: a 2020 peak (z-score 0.81) anchored by ERG mission statements and community-empowerment language, a 2023 trough (z-score –2.14), and a recovery to the highest point in the dataset by 2025–26 (z-scores 1.02 and 1.39). The 2022 copy introduced a 'Giving Back' section with concrete examples ('renovating houses for new mothers,' 'free coding classes to women in need') that persisted into later years, adding a community-service dimension to the altruism signal beyond the product mission statement.
